title: Typed function-call contracts and runtime validation for JSON parameter schemas
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Define a stable, typed JSON schema format for function/tool signatures exposed by the Core API and implement deterministic runtime parameter validation and clear error messages. This ticket covers the schema shape, validation semantics, error codes/messages, streaming/partial argument support, and a compatibility policy for older SDKs.

Background: Function-calling is increasingly used by customers to invoke external tools or structured internal actions. Current ad-hoc signatures lead to inconsistent validation behavior between SDKs and runtime, hard-to-debug errors, and incorrect fallbacks. We need a single on-wire contract that: 1) is machine-validated by the runtime, 2) supports expressive types (primitives, arrays, objects, enums), 3) expresses required vs optional semantics, defaulting rules, and 4) includes metadata that SDKs can use for client-side validation and typing generation.

Scope:
- Schema definition: propose a compact JSON schema subset (not full JSON Schema draft) tailored for tool calls. Fields: name, description, parameters (typed fields), required, examples, deprecated flag, stability (stable/beta/experimental). Types: string, integer, number, boolean, object, array, enum, union (via oneOf), and streaming marker for large binary/text payloads.
- Runtime validation: deterministic checks at request ingress that produce stable, documented error codes. Validation must run before dispatch to worker to avoid unnecessary compute charge for malformed calls.
- Error surface: standardized error codes and user-friendly messages mapping to client-side fixes. Include code categories: INVALID_SCHEMA (bad contract), INVALID_PARAMS (payload doesn't match contract), MISSING_REQUIRED, TYPE_MISMATCH, ENUM_VIOLATION, UNKNOWN_PARAM (extra fields), DEPRECATED_PARAM_USED, STREAMING_NOT_SUPPORTED. Each code includes suggested remediation text.
- Backwards compatibility: design a compatibility layer so older SDKs/clients that rely on looser semantics degrade gracefully. The runtime will support a compatibility mode header (X-Redwood-Compat-Version) and emit warnings when strict validation would have rejected a request. Provide deprecation windows and telemetry to track impacted clients.
- Streaming and partial args: specify how to represent arguments when the caller streams large inputs or when LLM emits partial structured output. Define a streaming parameter marker and how partial validation occurs (validate schema of completed chunks and accumulate until a final validate step).
- Developer ergonomics: include machine-readable examples for SDK generators, a JSON->TypeScript conversion guideline, and recommended error rendering for consoles.

Open design decisions:
1) Do we accept full JSON Schema draft-07 (flexible but heavy) or a constrained subset (lighter, faster to validate)? Proposal: constrained subset to avoid complexity and speed runtime validation.
2) Unknown extra keys: fail strictly by default, but allow clients to opt into permissive mode via header.
3) Streaming semantics: treat streaming fields as opaque until final chunk; partial validation will validate incremental chunks' shape where possible.

Deliverables:
- Specification doc (Confluence link in attachments) detailing schema, examples, and error codes.
- Runtime validator implementation behind feature flag + unit/integration tests.
- SDK guidelines and TypeScript generator sample.
- Migration guide for customers and internal rollout plan.

Risks:
- Breaking callers if strict mode enabled without sufficient compatibility telemetry. Mitigation: roll out in permissive-warning mode for 6 weeks, log top failing clients, then enable strict mode per client tier.

Acceptance criteria:
- Spec published and approved by API and SDK leads.
- Runtime validator merged behind flag and passing CI.
- Error codes documented in API reference and surfaced via structured error in responses.
- SDK sample generation demonstrates consistent types for a representative set of tool signatures.

Links: design doc and examples included in attachments. GitHub PRs will be linked in comments once opened.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Maya Chen: Initial proposal posted to #api-spec channel and Confluence (see attachment). Feedback request: prefer constrained subset vs full JSON Schema?
2026-03-06 - API Review (S. Alvarez): Recommend constrained subset; full JSON Schema has too many edge cases for runtime validation. Approved subset proposal with minor tweaks to union handling.

2026-03-08 - Amit Patel: Implemented validator prototype in runtime repo (branch: eng/ENG-5174/validator-proto). Uploaded unit test summary to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124 (WIP).

2026-03-10 - Security (I. Novak): Reviewed for injection/fuzzing concerns. Request: ensure strict parsing of strings to avoid JSON text-injection into command parameters and add fuzzer test. Marked security_review_required=true.
2026-03-12 - Design (L. Gomez): Suggested user-facing error copy for MISSING_REQUIRED and TYPE_MISMATCH to include field path and expected vs received types. Added example strings to description.

2026-03-14 - Amit Patel: Validator feature flagged as api.functioncall.validation.v1 and deployed to staging. Started collecting permissive-mode telemetry. Integration tests against mock SDKs running. Next: expand enum checks and streaming chunk validator.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Spec doc approved by API and SDK leads. 2) Runtime validator merged behind feature flag with unit & integration tests. 3) Error codes surfaced in API reference and sample SDK. 4) Permissive-to-strict rollout plan documented with telemetry hooks.
notes_for_qa: Test matrix should include: valid simple call, missing required param, type mismatch (string vs integer), enum violation, unknown extra key in strict/permissive mode, streaming large arg with partial chunks, deprecation-warning for deprecated param. Verify error codes and message templates match spec.
